title: The seesaw identity for the chain of theta lifts, and the index types of the data
summary: The seesaw identity `Data.seesaw`: there is a unit c ∈ ℂˣ, depending on D only, such that for every twist ϑ some good datum Ψ has ι_ϑ(𝒫(c·φ)) = B^Ψ_ϑ(φ) for all ramified columns φ (φ = 0 included; no further condition on φ), i.e. the indefinite chain of m theta lifts Y₀ → ⋯ → Y_m of the Poincaré series equals a finite admissible combination of definite chains X₀ → ⋯ → X_m restricted to Y_m; this is the input of Theorem A (`Data.short_forms`). It is proved by unfolding the chain one lift at a time against Bessel periods (exists_isAdmissibleComb_unfolding), each unfolded period being a finite sum over a cut of cosets whose multiplicities divide powers of the conductor of ϑ (exists_stage_cut, with the near-lines bounds of the lattices), evaluating pairs of lifts through zero terms of arrow pairs (AdmissibleEvaluation, EdgePair, DoubleLiftValue), and turning the resulting invariant admissible combination of reduced vacua into a good datum (GoodDatumExists). The folder also defines objects used across the proof: the places, characters, level prime N and index types of the data (IndexTypes), the lifts along the Y_j (GradingsOfY), the grid spaces (PairTensorData), and the Gauss-sum operator at the level prime used by the columns (NamesAtSplitLevel, LiftCharacters).
reader: claude (a Claude-side reader for the workspace grh-compact, following the reader's skill and contracts); statements, binder readings and claims written by hand from the Lean source at the pinned commit; ids, lines, hashes, quotations, spans and typed facts generated by reading/units/141/gen/gen.py; checked by `python3 tools/rb.py check 141` (line census, no Lean run)

members.name: IsAdmissibleComb
members.text: Definition. For a type α, a complex vector space Z, a family v : α → Z, a set A ⊆ α, natural numbers n and d, a proposition p, a real number B and z ∈ Z: IsAdmissibleComb(v, A, n, d, p, B, z) holds when z = ∑_x r(x)·v(x) for some finitely supported r : α → ℂ with IsAdmissibleCoeffs(A, n, d, p, B, r): the support of r lies in A, d·r(x) ∈ integralAway(n) for all x, and, if p holds, ∑_x |σ(r(x))| ≤ B for every automorphism σ of ℂ. In words: z is a finite combination of the v(x), x ∈ A, with coefficients integral away from n up to the denominator d, of size at most B at every conjugate when p holds.

members.text: Let n be a natural number and p a proposition; let α_j (j ∈ ℕ) be additive groups, F_j complex vector spaces, v_i : α_{2i} × α_{2i+1} → F_i, A_j ⊆ α_j additive subgroups, f_i ∈ F_i, d and m natural numbers and B real. members.name: IsAdmissibleComb.normUnit_smul
members.text: Let α be a type, Z a complex vector space, v : α → Z, A ⊆ α, n, d natural numbers with d ≠ 0 (hypothesis hd), p a proposition, B real, z ∈ Z, and C, a ∈ ℂ. If (premise) IsAdmissibleComb(x ↦ C·v(x), A, n, d, p, B, z), then IsAdmissibleComb(v, A, n, 1, p, d·B, normUnit(a·C/d)·a·z), where normUnit(w) = w⁻¹ for w ≠ 0 and normUnit(0) = 1. If a·C ≠ 0, the scalar normUnit(a·C/d)·a is d/C, which clears both the factor C and the denominator d. If a·C = 0, normUnit(a·C/d) = 1 and the vector normUnit(a·C/d)·a·z is 0 (for a = 0 directly; for C = 0 because z is a combination of the vectors C·v(x) = 0); e.g. a = 0, d = C = 1 and z ≠ 0 give the zero vector, not (d/C)·z. No hypothesis a·C ≠ 0 is made.

members.name: IsAdmissibleEval
members.text: Definition. For a CM field E with Weil data, finite index types ι, ι′, ι″, X, X′, μ, signs ε, ε′, ε″, hermitian spaces V, V′, V″, a prime N, a finite set P of places, β ∈ Ô, a map L on 𝒮(Hom(V′, V⁻ ⊕ V″)) and weights d (default selfOrConj(β)): IsAdmissibleEval(N, P, β, L, d) holds when there is C ∈ ℂ such that for every natural number n coprime to N, every proposition q (the q of ∀ n q is a proposition, under which the size bound is asked; the text reading also lists the section's finite type q and its instance, which the definition does not use: text-inferred pending Lean's signature) and every y ∈ weightedTranslations(n, (i, j) ↦ d_i): L(ϱ_f(y)·vac) satisfies IsAdmissibleComb(t ↦ C·τ_N(ϱ_f(t₁)vac ⊗ ϱ_f(t₂)vac), translations(n, β̄) × translations(n, β̄), n, |((X ⊔ {pt}) ⊔ (μ ⊔ {pt})) × X′ → Ô/β|, q, 1, L(ϱ_f(y)vac)), where τ_N = translateSum(X, X′, P, N, μ). In words: evaluated vacua are admissible combinations (size 1 under q, denominator |Ô/β|^{(|X|+|μ|+2)|X′|}) of C times τ_N of pairs of translated vacua.

members.text: Let E be a CM field with Weil data, X, X′, X₀ finite index types, κ, e, e′, e″ weights, O a type, a, b : O → characters of U(1)(𝔸), and for every o linear maps k(o), k′(o) that are theta lifts X → X′ for rankTwist(a(o)) (hk) and X′ → X₀ for rankTwist(b(o)) (hk′) in the sense of `Space.IsThetaLift`. members.name: zeroTermFin
members.text: Definition. Let E be a field with a CM type and Weil data, n, n₀, p finite index types, V and V₀ hermitian spaces over E (basis indices n, n₀; signs s, s₀) and D a splitting of V over V₀ along p (`Space.Splitting`). zeroTermFin(D) is the continuous linear map f ↦ zeroTerm_D(v ⊗ f) from 𝒮(V) to 𝒮(V₀): v is the Fock vacuum moved by the real point of a chosen element adapted to D (`Splitting.exists_isAdapted_and_frame_eq` with t = 1), v ⊗ f = `Space.integrated` v f = ∫ v(y)ϱ(y)f dy, and zeroTerm_D is the zero term along the isotropic frame k (`Splitting.zeroTerm`: the mean of f(ιy + kb) over b ∈ 𝔸^p/E^p). It is the finite part of the constant term.

members.name: GradeZeroPart
members.text: Definition (structure). For a field E with a CM type, finite index types ι, ι″, signs ε, ε″, hermitian spaces V (indices ι) and V″ (indices ι″) and weights wt : ι → ℤ, a GradeZeroPart(V, V″, wt) consists of an injection index : ι″ ↪ ι whose image is exactly {i : wt(i) = 0} (mem_range_index); a matrix incl ∈ M_{ι×ι″}(E) with incl(a, b) = 0 whenever wt(a) ≠ 0 (incl_eq_zero) and inclᴴ·J_V·incl = J_{V″} (gram_incl); and the condition that J_V pairs only opposite weights: J_V(a, b) ≠ 0 implies wt(a) + wt(b) = 0 (grade_add). So incl is a rational isometry from V″ into the span of the basis vectors of weight 0.

For a field E with a CM type and Weil data, gradings Y of V (X, s), Y′ of V′ (X′, s′), Y″ of V″ (X₀, s″) of norm N and finite index types X″, q, an ArrowPair(X″, q, Y, Y′, Y″) consists of: zeroPart, a grade-zero part of V⁻ ⊕ V″ for the weights gradeOf_Y ⊔ gradeOf_{Y″}, whose zero part is the sum of q hyperbolic planes and X⁻ ⊕ X″ (hypSum q (flipSum X X″)); string_spec: s odd, s′ = s − 1, s″ = s′ − 1, and the constant c of Y′ equals that of Y; even_card_add: |ι| + |ι″| even; embX : U(X₀) → U(X″), a homomorphism of adelic unitary groups with det(embX k) = det k (det_embX); intertwines: diag(ratCoord inclX_Y(g), ratCoord inclX_{Y″}(k))·incl = incl·(1 ⊕ g⁻ ⊕ embX(k)) for g ∈ U(X), k ∈ U(X₀) (the identification is compatible with U(X) × U(X₀)); gradeOne : q ↪ {indices l of V′ with gradeOf_{Y′}(l) = 1}; and stackedT_apply: stackedT(Y, Y′, Y″)(index a, l) = ∑_k [l = gradeOne k]·incl(index a, (k-th dual hyperbolic vector))·c(Y′).

members.name: middlePair
members.text: Definition. For a field E with a CM type and Weil data, gradings Y of V (X, s), Y′ of V′ (X′, s′), Y″ of V″ (X₀, s″) of norm N with s odd, s′ = s − 1, s″ = s′ − 1 and equal constants c (H), |ι| + |ι″| even (H′) and s ≠ 1 (h): the ArrowPair(X₀, {pt}, Y, Y′, Y″) that removes one hyperbolic plane, spanned by the middle vectors z of Y and z″ of Y″. members.name: Data.TameChar
members.text: Definition (structure). For admissible data D, a tame character consists of a character toAutChar of U(1)(𝔸) trivial on U(1)(E), a finite set Q of finite places and a family ψ of residue characters such that the character has weight 0 and tame part ψ (hasWeight), ψ_w = 1 for w ∉ Q (ψ_eq_one), w̄ ∉ Q for w ∈ Q (star_notMem), and g₀g₁N is coprime to ∏_{w∈Q} N(w) (coprime, the seventh field). Nothing is asked of ψ_w for w ∈ Q: a tame character may mark a place of Q at which its tame part is trivial; the non-triviality at every marked place is the extra field of `Data.Twist`.

members.name: coverMultiplicity
members.text: Definition. For a group H, subgroups S, A, J of H, a finite set T of left cosets of J and a coset t ∈ H/J: coverMultiplicity(S, A, T, t) is the number of left cosets r(S ∩ A) ∈ S/(S ∩ A) that have some representative r ∈ S with r⁻¹·t ∈ T (equivalently t ∈ r·T), i.e. the cardinality of the image of {r ∈ S : r⁻¹·t ∈ T} in S/(S ∩ A), counted as 0 if it is infinite. When T is stable under S ∩ A the condition does not depend on the representative.

members.name: exists_cut_coverMultiplicity_dvd
members.text: Let E be a field with a CM type, ι a finite index type, S, A, J, B subgroups of G_f(ι) with A, J levels (k, o), J ≤ A (l) and A ≤ B (b), D ⊆ G_f(ι) compact (cD), q a natural number and W a property of elements. Assume hD: every x ∈ D lies in B and has n with (x u x⁻¹)^{q^n} ∈ A for all u ∈ J; and hW: for every x with W(x) some r ∈ S has r·x ∈ D. Then there is a finite set T of cosets of J such that (i) T is stable under S ∩ A (for p ∈ S with p ∈ A: t ∈ T ⟺ p·t ∈ T); (ii) every x with xJ ∈ T lies in B; (iii) for every x with xJ ∈ T or W(x), coverMultiplicity(S, A, T, xJ) divides q^j for some j.

members.name: Grading.exists_integral_eq_sum_over_cut
members.text: Let E be a field with a CM type and Weil data, V a hermitian space (indices ι, signs ε) with a grading Y (X plus a string of length s, norm N), A a level (k) and a a function on the real points. There is κ ∈ ℂ such that for every function P on the adelic unitary group G, every y automorphic on V, every level J, every finite set T of cosets of J and every b : G_f/J → ℂ the following holds. If P is generic for Y (`Grading.IsGeneric`), y is automorphic, f = P·y is integrable for the measure computing integrals over B(E⁺)\G (B = `Grading.besselGroup`, B(E⁺) its rational points `Grading.ratBessel`), T is stable under B_f ∩ A (B_f = `Grading.besselFin`), coverMultiplicity(B_f, A, T, g_f J) ≠ 0 whenever f(g) ≠ 0, and ∫_{[B]} f(r·t) dr = [K₀ : J]·a(t_∞)·b(t_f J) for every t with t_f J ∈ T, then ∫_{B(E⁺)\G} f = κ·∑_{t∈T} b(t)/coverMultiplicity(B_f, A, T, t).

members.name: gradedLatticeBasis
members.text: Definition. Let R be a commutative ring with an involution r ↦ r̄, X′ and ι index types, s a natural number, e : (X′ ⊔ {pt}) ⊔ {0, …, s−1} ≃ ι a bijection, a and π units of R, and u a unitary element of R (u·ū = 1). gradedLatticeBasis(e, a, π, u) is the ι × ι matrix obtained by relabelling rows and columns along e from the block matrix, for the decomposition (X′ ⊔ {pt}) ⊔ {0, …, s−1} of rows and columns: upper left block the identity if s is even, and diag(1 on X′, π̄⁻¹ at pt) if s is odd; upper right block 0; lower left block zero except in the column pt, where the row of the string index b has u·(π̄π)⁻¹ if b = s−1−b (the middle index z, which exists only for s odd) and 0 otherwise; lower right block diagonal, with entry u at every string index if s is odd, and, if s is even, u·a⁻¹ at the b with 2b < s and u·ā at the other b. In words: a basis matrix whose string rows are multiplied by u; for odd s the identity with the column of the point e replaced by e/π̄ + z/(ππ̄), for even s diag(1; a⁻¹, …, a⁻¹, ā, …, ā).

members.name: IsSplitLevel
members.text: Definition (class). For a field E with a CM type, a finite set P of finite places of E and a natural number N, IsSplitLevel(P, N) holds when (star_notMem) w̄ ∉ P for every w ∈ P; (q_eq) every w ∈ P has absolute norm N; (v_natCast) N has valuation exp(−1) in E_w, i.e. N is a uniformiser at w, for every w ∈ P; and (natCast_mem_iff) a finite place w divides N exactly when w ∈ P or w̄ ∈ P. So the places above N are those of P ∪ P̄, each of norm N with uniformiser N.

members.name: residueOverN
members.text: Definition. For a number field E, a finite set P of finite places, a natural number N and y ∈ (ℤ/N)^P: residueOverN(y) is the finite adele with component ỹ_w/N at w ∈ P, ỹ_w ∈ {0, …, N−1} the least non-negative representative of y_w, and 0 at the places outside P (extension by zero). The definition accepts every natural number N; the description by representatives in {0, …, N−1} is for N > 0. For N = 0, ZMod 0 = ℤ and division by 0 in the local field gives 0, so residueOverN(y) = 0.

members.name: IsSplitLevel.reduction_eq_iff
members.text: For a field E with a CM type, a split level P for the prime N (instance Λ), x ∈ O (integral elements of ∏_{w∈P} E_w) and c ∈ (ℤ/N)^P: reduction(x) = c if and only if for every w ∈ P, (x_w − c̃_w)/N is integral in E_w (valuation ≤ 1), c̃_w the least non-negative representative. (One simpa: the residue of x_w − c̃_w is zero iff x_w − c̃_w lies in the maximal ideal, generated by the uniformiser N.)

members.name: IsSplitLevel.fourierOp
members.text: Definition. For a field E with a CM type and Weil data, a split level P for the prime N (instance Λ), a finite index type n and a representation π of GL_{n+1}(∏_{w∈P} E_w): fourierOp(π) = π(u₀)·∑_y psiN(y_last)·π(κ_y), the sum over the vectors y ∈ ((ℤ/N)^P)^{n+1} whose last entry y_last is a unit of (ℤ/N)^P, where u₀ = diagNInv and κ_y = inclGL(liftGL(k(y))) is an integral invertible matrix whose reduction has last column and last row y (k from exists_GL_last_col_and_row). A Gauss-sum Hecke operator: Fourier transform in the last row, followed by u₀.

members.name: IsSplitLevel.LiftLaw
members.text: Definition (structure). Let E be a field with a CM type and Weil data, P a split level for the prime N (instance IsSplitLevel P N, which Lean takes as an argument), π, π′ representations of GL_{n+1} and GL_{n′+1} over ∏_{w∈P} E_w, L a ℂ-linear map from functions on (n′+1) × (n+1) matrices over ∏ E_w to Hom(π, π′), and γ ∈ ℂ. LiftLaw(π, π′, L, γ) holds when (integral_equivariant) for all a ∈ GL_{n+1}(O), b ∈ GL_{n′+1}(O), every function f of residue matrices and every φ: π′(b)·(L[liftFn(T ↦ f(red(b)·T·red(a)))](π(a)φ)) = L[liftFn f]φ, red the reduction modulo N; and (diagNInv_law) π′(u₀)(L[𝐞]φ) = γ·L[𝐛_e](π(u₀)φ) for every φ, with 𝐞 = lastRowDatum, 𝐛_e = lastColDatum of the last basis vector and u₀ = diagNInv.

members.name: IsSplitLevel.pairWeilFinite_name
members.text: For a field E with a CM type and Weil data, a split level P for the prime N (instance h), g ∈ GL_n(∏_{w∈P} E_w), k ∈ GL_{n′}(∏ E_w), a function f on n′ × n matrices, characters a, b of U(1)(𝔸) and a finite datum v: the pair Weil operator with characters a, b of (embedGL g, embedGL k) sends name(liftFn f)(v) to (detCharAt(b.spaceChar(|n′|), |n′|)(g)⁻¹·detCharAt(a.spaceChar(|n|), |n|)(k))·name(S ↦ f̃(k⁻¹·S·g))(v), the factors in this order, where f̃ = liftFn(f) is the local lift of f (f̃(S) = f(S mod N) for integral S over ∏_{w∈P} E_w and 0 otherwise). The change of variables S ↦ k⁻¹·S·g acts on the lifted function f̃, not inside the residue function f: g and k are general elements of the local general linear groups and can move a matrix into or out of the integral locus, so S ↦ f̃(k⁻¹·S·g) is in general not liftFn(S ↦ f(k⁻¹·S·g)).

members.name: exists_branching_pairing
members.text: Let E be a CM field, n a non-empty and n′ a finite index type, κ, κ′ weights, e, e′ determinant exponents, l′ and l doubled Harish-Chandra parameters on n′ and n with IsHCParam(κ, e, l′) (h) and IsHCParam(κ′, e′, −l) (h′), interlacing: #{j : x < l′_w(j)} − #{i : x < l_w(i)} ∈ {0, 1} for every place w and x (hi); and let σ : n ⊔ {pt} ≃ n′ with signs s on n, r on pt, t on n′ such that (s ⊔ r)∘σ⁻¹ = t (hσ) and t = 1 (ht). Write v′ ⬝ (B·v) = (v′)ᵀ·B·v for the bilinear pairing given by B (the dot product ⬝, no complex conjugation). Then there is an integer matrix B such that (a) there are integers N_τ with (ρ_{κ′,e′}(g)v′) ⬝ (B·ρ_{κ,e}(diag_σ(g, u))v) = ∏_τ det(u_τ)^{N_τ}·(v′ ⬝ (B·v)) for all commutative rings S with involution, fields R of characteristic 0, ring maps f_τ : S → R and g, u, v′, v (ρ = weylRep, entries mapped by f); |N_τ| ≤ boxes(κ, |n′|) + |e_τ|; and |v′ ⬝ (B·v)| ≤ (M^M)³·√weylNormSq(v′)·√weylNormSq(v) (the norms of the positive definite Weyl Gram form) for every M ≥ boxes(κ, |n′|); and (b) for every g there is c = c_g (chosen after g and before V, η, φ, u and K; c_g = 0 is not excluded) such that for every standard space V (indices n, signs s), all algebraic forms η of weight (κ′, e′) and φ of weight (κ, e), every u and every level K: ∫_{[U(V)]} F_η^{(−l, s)}(x)·F_φ^{(l′, t)}(σ-block(x, 1, u)·(g, 1)) dx = c_g/[K₀ : K]·(the class integral at level K of h ↦ η(h) ⬝ (B·φ(diag_σ(h, u)))), F = ofAlgForm. So B pairs the two weights bilinearly and invariantly up to a power of det u, with explicit bounds, and periods over definite U(n) are constants times means of this pairing.

members.name: Data.seesaw
members.text: The seesaw identity. For admissible data D there is a unit c ∈ ℂˣ (a non-zero complex number) such that for every twist ϑ there is a finitely supported family Ψ : Translations(D) →₀ ℂ with IsGoodDatum(ϑ, Ψ) and ι_ϑ(𝒫(c·φ)) = B^Ψ_ϑ(φ) for every ramified column φ ∈ D.ramifiedColumns, the image of the ramifying operator ∏_{w∣π}(1 − z_w) on Column(D) (φ is any element of that subspace, φ = 0 included, read in Column(D) through the inclusion `ramifiedColumns.subtype`; no shortness, integrality or non-vanishing condition on φ). Here 𝒫 = `Data.poincare` is the Poincaré series (columns on X₀ → forms of principal level on Y₀), ι_ϑ = `Data.ι` ϑ is the chain of the m = 2ϱ + 2 theta lifts through Y₀, …, Y_m (each lift liftY carrying its level-index scalar [K₀ : levelY(ϑ, j)]) followed by the identification with algebraic forms on Y_m, and B^Ψ_ϑ = `Data.Bμ` ϑ Ψ is the combination ∑_x Ψ(x)·(chain of m definite lifts X₀ → ⋯ → X_m with the data translateDatum(x)) followed by the restriction to Y_m (`Data.restrictToY`: restriction to the points diag(h, 1), the branching matrix, and the factor ∏_τ τ(π̄)^{−D.branchExp(τ)}). IsGoodDatum(ϑ, Ψ) (unit 145) says: Ψ is supported on admissibleTranslations(levelNorm(ϑ)·N) (π_g·t_k integral at every place not dividing levelNorm(ϑ)·N), coefficients Ψ(t) in integralAway(levelNorm(ϑ)) (denominator 1), ∑_t |σ(Ψ(t))| ≤ exp(x^60) for every automorphism σ of ℂ when Q(ϑ) = ∅, joint invariance, and chain_at_N (the definite chain of Ψ is the combination of the paired chains with the data pairTranslates of the projections at the places above π); the two moduli, levelNorm(ϑ)·N and levelNorm(ϑ), differ by the level prime N. The unit c is chosen before the quantifier over twists, so it depends on D only, not on ϑ or φ; one Ψ (depending on ϑ) serves all ramified columns at once. Lean gives no bound on |c|.
